S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (dysthymia) is a chronic mood disorder characterized by a consistently low or dysthymic mood lasting at least two years in adults, with no extended periods of full remission. Individuals often function day-to-day but at a reduced level, experiencing a long-standing sense of gloom, low motivation, and other depressive features that become part of their perceived personality. Clinically, it differs from major depressive disorder by its chronicity and typically milder, more insidious presentation, though episodes of major depression can occur on top of it ("double depression"). It is frequently under-recognized because patients and families may attribute the symptoms to character or life circumstances rather than a treatable illness, and impairment is often seen in social, occupational, or academic domains over time.

patient.stressor: Clifford began a phased retirement a little over three years ago, shifting from full-time IT leadership to a part-time advisory role and then officially retiring sooner than he had planned when his company restructured. At first he welcomed the chance to fish more and tend his garden, but as months passed he struggled to find a sense of purpose comparable to managing complex systems and mentoring younger staff, and he became increasingly preoccupied with whether he was still useful or "keeping up" with rapid changes in technology. Over the next 2 years and 4 months, he gradually withdrew from some community activities, started missing routine appointments, and found that even tinkering with vintage hardware and volunteering with the youth robotics club felt more like obligations than sources of satisfaction, yet he downplayed this as just getting older. His wife eventually insisted he bring it up at a checkup after he mentioned that most days felt like he was just going through the motions and that even planning simple road trips or attending church concerts seemed like more effort than they were worth, leading to a referral for mental health evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: I’m just tired all the time and don’t have the energy to do much of anything anymore, even the stuff I used to enjoy.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I just feel this low, gray cloud hanging over me, like nothing is exactly wrong but nothing feels worth getting excited about either, and I catch myself thinking, 'what’s the point?' even when I’m out fishing or sitting with my grandkids.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: Ever since I stopped working full-time, my appetite’s been all over the place—some days I realize it’s three in the afternoon and I’ve barely eaten a sandwich because I just don’t feel interested in food, and then other nights I’ll mindlessly plow through a bag of chips in front of the TV even though I’m not really hungry.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: I go to bed around ten, but I’ll lie there for an hour or more with my mind spinning about how I’m falling behind in tech or wasting my retirement, and then I wake up at four or five in the morning for no good reason and just stare at the ceiling feeling worn out but unable to fall back asleep.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: It feels like someone turned my internal battery down to half-power—just taking care of the house, going to the store, or driving to a doctor’s appointment leaves me wiped out, and even things I used to look forward to, like working on old computers or helping the robotics kids, now feel like a chore I have to push myself through.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Over the past couple of years I’ve let things slide—I’ve backed out of a lot of community stuff, missed more appointments than I’d like to admit, and even around the house my wife ends up picking up the slack because I just can’t seem to keep up with what I used to handle without thinking.
add_requirements.duration: Looking back, this low, worn-out way I’ve been feeling really settled in not long after I started phasing into retirement and has pretty much stuck with me ever since.
